```python
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots for a clean, modern look
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a PairGrid for a more customized pairplot-like visualization
g = sns.PairGrid(df, hue="species", corner=True, diag_sharey=False)

# Use different plots for the diagonal and off-diagonal elements
# Diagonal: Kernel Density Estimate to show the distribution of each feature per species
g.map_diag(sns.kdeplot, fill=True, lw=2)

# Off-diagonal: Scatter plots to show relationships between pairs of features
g.map_lower(sns.scatterplot, s=50, alpha=0.8, edgecolor='w')

# Add a single, clear legend to the figure
g.add_legend(title="Species", loc="upper right")

# Adjust spacing and add a comprehensive title
g.fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.92)
g.fig.suptitle('Distribution and Pairwise Relationships of Iris Flower Measurements', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
```
